title: Embedding dims & throughput: VDB integration discovery
summary: Initial discovery to scope an embeddings + rerank POC. Customer wants to understand tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, expected QPS/throughput, embedding dimensionality and storage costs, and vector DB integration patterns (hybrid search + rerank). Redwood AE/SE outlined autoscaling, batching, KV/prefix cache, and suggested benchmark plan with sample dataset and latency targets.
next_steps: Redwood to share hosted vs dedicated pricing estimator and costs for 1536/2048-dim embeddings
SE to run a small benchmark plan with LatticeSearch sample dataset (expected 100 QPS, 128 token avg) by 2025-07-25
Send SOC2 and KMS integration docs + network diagram for Redwood Private/VPC
Schedule technical deep dive around vector DB connectors (Milvus/Pinecone) w/ Sandeep for 2025-07-22
action_items: Priya Shah: Send pricing estimator + short summary deck (due 2025-07-18)
Michael Chen: Draft benchmark plan and required artifacts (sample data format, scripts) (due 2025-07-20)
Dana Li: Share 1k sample vectors and queries to run initial eval (due 2025-07-18)
Sandeep Patel: Confirm network constraints for Private deployment and provide firewall/egress rules (due 2025-07-21)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-16 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Michael Chen (Redwood SE), Ava Miller (Redwood Solutions), Tom Reyes (LatticeSearch Head of Search), Dana Li (ML Eng), Sandeep Patel (Infra)

[00:00] Priya Shah: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — quick round of intros?

[00:08] Tom Reyes: Yeah hi Tom here, I run the search team at LatticeSearch. We're exploring vector search for product search + support rerank.

[00:14] Dana Li: Dana, ML eng on the team, primarily embedding pipelines and model infra.

[00:20] Sandeep Patel: Sandeep, infra — I'll be the one worrying about network and deployment.

[00:26] Priya Shah: Great. Michael and I from Redwood — Michael focuses on performance and infra, I'll lead commercial & next steps.

[00:35] Michael Chen: Quick agenda: understand current stack, targets (qps/latency), vector DB choices, embedding dims, then sketch a POC and security needs.

[00:44] Tom Reyes: Sound good. For context we currently use Elasticsearch for lexical and a small Faiss cluster for research. We want to move to a production vector DB and add an LLM-based reranker — that's where Redwood comes in. Main questions: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; how many dimensions to use; cost/latency tradeoffs at 100 QPS and spikes to ~400 QPS.

[01:08] Michael Chen: Perfect. Can you share current vector size and fleet?

[01:12] Dana Li: Today embeddings are 1536 dims from an open model, roughly 12M vectors. Peak query rate on search endpoints is about 80–120 qps for product search and support combined; tail spikes during campaigns. We expect growth.

[01:30] Priya Shah: 12M is a healthy corpus. For 1536 dims stored in a vector DB there are storage and index tradeoffs — product solutions vary. Are you planning hybrid search — lexical filter + vector candidate retrieval + LLM rerank?

[01:46] Tom Reyes: Exactly, we want hybrid. Lexical filter to narrow to ~1000 candidates, vectordb kNN to 100 candidates, then rerank top 10 with LLM. Latency budget for the whole flow is ~200–300ms p50 and 600ms p95 ideally.

[02:06] Michael Chen: Ok. Hosted Redwood can meet the LLM rerank latency with streaming and batching; dedicated gives more predictable throughput and lower p95 when you pin capacity; private gives full network control but requires heavier setup. For the rerank step, the model size and quantization matter — are you considering smaller quantized models or a larger model?

[02:27] Dana Li: We're leaning to a dense 7B quantized model for rerank to keep costs manageable but need quality. Curious about Redwood's recommendations for embedding dims — 1536 vs 2048 — we see quality gains but cost increase.

[02:42] Michael Chen: 2048 can help in some semantic tasks, but storage grows linearly and nearest neighbor index memory increases. There's also impact on retrieval latency and vector DB cost (index size). With Redwood's Optimize suggestions we can simulate lower-dim runs or run PCA/OPQ to shrink vectors while preserving quality. Also batching and KV/prefix cache can amortize token costs for rerank.

[03:10] Tom Reyes: Can you expand on KV cache? I've seen mention in Redwood docs but not sure how it helps rerank flows.

[03:16] Michael Chen: Sure. For autoregressive decoders it's more for generation; for rerank we really leverage request-level caching when queries repeat and prefix caching if rerank uses overlapping history. For vector retrieval the big wins are index caching in the vdb and reusing embeddings if same doc vectors are requested. Redwood also has smart routing — if Dedicated is down we can fallback to hosted smaller model.

[03:42] Sandeep Patel: About Private: we have strict egress rules and need KMS/HSM integration with our own keys. How does Redwood handle that?

[03:50] Priya Shah: For Private we provide a control plane that can sit in your VPC and support customer-managed KMS; we have HSM integrations for enterprise plans. We'll share our security packet. Hosted still supports encryption at rest + in transit and SOC2 compliance but no BYOK unless on Dedicated/Private.

[04:12] Tom Reyes: Good. For vector DBs, we're evaluating Pinecone and Milvus. Any pointers on connectors or patterns? Do customers run vectordb alongside Redwood or behind Redwood in routing?

[04:26] Michael Chen: Both patterns exist. Typical architecture: Redwood serves the rerank/LLM stage and your vector DB (Milvus/Pinecone/Weaviate) handles nearest neighbor. Redwood can call the DB as an external service; or if you want lower hops you can co-locate Redwood Dedicated near the DB. For latency tight setups, Dedicated + colocated DB in same AZ, with VPC peering, is common. For hosted, additional network hops to external vectordb may add 20–50ms depending on region.

[04:58] Dana Li: For our target 200–300ms overall p50, what's realistic if we keep the DB in our cloud account and use Redwood hosted?

[05:06] Michael Chen: If vectordb lives in your account in same region and you use hosted Redwood endpoints in same region, you can be in the ballpark p50 200–300ms but p95 will be sensitive to network and DB indexing choices. Dedicated tends to tighten p95. We'll need to benchmark with your actual index settings.

[05:30] Tom Reyes: We're also worried about the dimensionality storage costs — can Redwood give estimates for token costs on rerank plus storage impact for 12M vectors at 1536 vs 2048 dims?

[05:42] Priya Shah: Yes — action item: we'll send a cost estimator. Generally storage scales by dimension * N * 4 bytes (float32) unless you quantize; many vector DBs use compressed indexes. For embeddings we often recommend experimenting with 1536 then try OPQ or product quantization to save 4–8x. We'll include those assumptions in the estimator.

[06:05] Sandeep Patel: Are there support SLAs for Dedicated? We'd like 99.9 and runbooks.

[06:11] Priya Shah: Dedicated has SLA tiers — 99.9 is available on enterprise plan with support runbooks. We'll surface the options in the pricing doc.

[06:22] Michael Chen: Let's talk about benchmark plan — propose you share 1k representative queries + 1k candidate docs and we'll run three configs: Hosted (standard), Dedicated (pinned capacity), and a quantized model option. We'll measure end-to-end latency including vectordb call. Is that acceptable?

[06:42] Dana Li: Yes. We'll share data but need to obfuscate PII. We can send synthetic or hashed IDs.

[06:48] Tom Reyes: On security, can you provide audit logs and role-based access controls?

[06:53] Priya Shah: Yes — RBAC and audit logs are part of the Console. For Private deployments you can integrate with your SAML/SSO and central audit. We'll attach sample screenshots and doc.

[07:06] Sandeep Patel: Network diagram for Private please, and any required firewall ports. Also what ports for DB connectivity?

[07:12] Michael Chen: We'll include egress/ingress requirements. Typical: GRPC/HTTPS to Redwood control plane, and DB-specific ports (Milvus 19530, etc.) depending on connector. We'll put specifics in the network doc.

[07:28] Tom Reyes: One more — model versioning and rollouts: if we change reranker models, can we A/B and rollback?

[07:34] Priya Shah: Yes — Redwood Console supports rollouts, canary percentages, automatic fallback to previous model if latency or quality regresses, and you can tie to prompt-level evals. We'll demo that in the deep dive.

[07:48] Michael Chen: Small note on quality metrics — for rerank please tell us which metrics matter: MRR@10, NDCG, or hit-rate? That will shape the eval.

[07:57] Dana Li: NDCG@10 and latency p95 are primary, plus some manual quality checks for edge cases.

[08:04] Priya Shah: Great — we'll bake that into the benchmark. Next steps and timelines — we propose: pricing deck and security docs by 2025-07-18, benchmark plan by 2025-07-20, and a technical deep dive with Sandeep on 2025-07-22.

[08:20] Tom Reyes: Works for us. Any recommended embedding dimensionality baseline?

[08:25] Michael Chen: Start at 1536 since you already have it, run a PCA/quantization experiment to simulate 768/1024 and compare. If you need extra semantic expressivity try 2048 but expect ~33% storage increase. We'll show simulations in the benchmark.

[08:44] Dana Li: On cost controls — can Redwood apply rate limits per token and per-route? We want to avoid runaway rerank costs during spikes.

[08:51] Priya Shah: Yes — Console supports per-key quotas, per-route throttles, and token cost breakdowns. You can set hard caps and alerts.

[08:58] Sandeep Patel: Any notes around isolation — if we choose Dedicated will we get a physically isolated pool?

[09:04] Michael Chen: Dedicated provides a reserved GPU pool for your account; it's logically isolated and offers predictability. For strict tenancy you can pair Dedicated with Private deployment. We'll detail isolation guarantees in the contract appendix.

[09:20] Tom Reyes: That helps. Alright let's recap and confirm action items.

[09:25] Priya Shah: Recap: Redwood to send pricing estimator, security + network docs, benchmark plan; customer to share sample vectors/queries and clarify throughput windows. We'll schedule deep dive. Anything else?

[09:37] Dana Li: Please include example scripts for embedding extraction and a minimal runner for rerank tests — that'll help speed POC.

[09:44] Michael Chen: Will do — include a small repo and runbook.

[09:48] Tom Reyes: Thanks everyone, this was useful.

[09:52] Priya Shah: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.

[09:58] (call ends)
recording_notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and generic speaker labels, some product names abbreviated (vectordb, KMS written as K-M-S in transcript). References to ports and Milvus default port mentioned informally.
notes_for_sales: Customer is a mid-stage startup with 12M vectors and immediate interest in a 3-week POC. High chance to move to Dedicated if p95 and cost targets align. Security constraints (BYOK/HSM, egress) push towards Private for longer-term. Prioritize bench plan and pricing estimator. Mention support for RBAC, audit logs, and rollouts in follow up docs.
